docs.title: Internet Topology Pipeline
docs.text:
Reconstruct the Internet's AS-level topology from publicly available BGP routing data published by RIPE NCC's Routing Information Service (RIS) and RouteViews.

The pipeline downloads MRT RIB snapshot files from route collectors, extracts AS paths, and produces a deduplicated edge list where each line is a pair of ASNs observed to be directly connected:

00001299 00003356
00001299 00022773
00003356 00015169

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
BGP routers exchange reachability information as AS paths — ordered sequences of Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) that a route traverses. The path 1299 3356 15169 means links exist between AS 1299↔3356 and AS 3356↔15169.

RIPE RIS operates a global network of route collectors (rrc00–rrc25), each peering with many BGP routers. Periodically, each collector dumps a full snapshot of its routing table into an MRT-format binary file. This pipeline processes those snapshots to reconstruct the observed AS-level topology.

RouteViews provides additional vantage points across ~40 collectors worldwide, processed identically to RIS data.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Purpose Install Python 3.12+ Runtime uv manages this uv Python package manager curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh just Pipeline orchestration cargo install just or system package bgpreader MRT file parser Part of BGPStream; install via system package bash 4+ Required for collect.sh macOS: brew install bash

macOS bash

macOS ships with bash 3.2. The collect.sh fleet script requires bash 4+ for export -f. Install a newer version with brew install bash. This is only needed on the central machine that runs collect; remote nodes only need ssh and rsync.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/carlos-cagnazzo/internet-topology-ris
cd internet-topology-ris
uv sync

Verify bgpreader is available:

bgpreader --version

docs.title: Pipeline at a Glance
docs.text:
get-mrt.py          ──┐
                       ├──▶  extract-paths.py  ──▶  build-topology.py
get-routeviews.py   ──┘
  1. Download — fetch 00:00 UTC RIB snapshots (.gz from RIS, .bz2 from RouteViews)
  2. Extract — run bgpreader on each file, write per-file AS path lists
  3. Build — read all path files, extract edges, deduplicate, write topology

See Quick Start to run it, or Pipeline for a deep dive.

docs.title: Fleet Workflow
docs.text: Processing a full day of data (all RIS collectors + RouteViews) can take several hours on a single machine. The fleet workflow distributes download and extraction across multiple machines, then merges the results centrally.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Central: just dispatch
  → Node A: tmux slice-20260701-20260715  (rrc00-rrc12, serially)
  → Node B: tmux slice-20260716-20260731  (rrc13-rrc25, serially)
  → Node B: tmux slice-20260801-20260815  (rrc13-rrc25, serially)  ← parallel session

Central: just status            # check progress at any time

Central: just date='202607*' collect
Central: just date='202607*' topology

Each fleet node runs slice (download RIS + RouteViews + extract paths) for its assigned dates independently. The central machine dispatches, monitors, collects, and builds the final topology.

docs.title: 1. Create fleet.csv
docs.text:
cp fleet/fleet.csv.example fleet.csv

Format: username,hostname,/absolute/path/to/repo — one machine per line.

# username,hostname,repo_path
carlos,gauss.xt6labs.io,/home/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris
carlos,node2.example.com,/home/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris
carlos,mac.local,/Users/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris

fleet.csv is gitignored — specific to your deployment. The fleet/fleet.csv.example template is tracked.

docs.title: 2. Create assignments.csv
docs.text:
cp fleet/assignments.csv.example assignments.csv

Format: hostname,start_date,end_date,collectors — one line per tmux session.

# hostname,start_date,end_date,collectors
gauss.xt6labs.io,20260701,20260715,rrc00-rrc12
gauss.xt6labs.io,20260720,20260725,rrc00-rrc12
node2.example.com,20260716,20260719,rrc13-rrc25
node2.example.com,20260726,20260731,rrc13-rrc25
  • One line = one tmux session on that host, iterating its date range serially
  • Multiple lines per host = multiple parallel sessions on that host
  • Ranges can be discontinuous — just add more lines
  • assignments.csv is gitignored; edit it freely without committing. Template at fleet/assignments.csv.example

docs.title: 3. Ensure SSH access
docs.text:
All machines must be reachable with a shared SSH key from the central machine:

ssh carlos@gauss.xt6labs.io "echo ok"

docs.title: 4. Clone the repo on each node
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/carlos-cagnazzo/internet-topology-ris \
  /home/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris

docs.title: Dispatching work
docs.text:
just dispatch           # dispatch all assigned sessions (2 parallel SSH connections)
just jobs=4 dispatch    # more parallelism

For each line in assignments.csv, dispatch.sh:

  1. Looks up user and repo from fleet.csv
  2. SSHes to the node and checks whether a tmux session named slice-START-END already exists
  3. If not: writes a dated slice script to /tmp/dispatch-slice-START-END.sh on the remote and starts it in a new tmux session

The session runs a loop like: 

cd /repo && git pull -q
for d in 20260701 20260702 … 20260715; do
    just date=$d collectors=rrc00-rrc12 slice
done

slice is self-contained: it downloads RIS collectors, downloads RouteViews, and extracts paths — all for that date.

Re-running just dispatch is safe — sessions that already exist are skipped.

docs.title: Checking progress
docs.text:
just status

SSHes to each assigned host in one round-trip, checks running tmux sessions and existing paths/ directories, and prints a table:

gauss.xt6labs.io
  slice-20260701-20260715  rrc00-rrc12    [running  8/15]
     20260701✓  20260702✓  20260703✓  20260704✓  20260705✓  20260706✓  20260707✓
     20260708✓  20260709·  20260710·  20260711·  20260712·  20260713·  20260714·
     20260715·

node2.example.com
  slice-20260716-20260719  rrc13-rrc25    [done     4/4]
     20260716✓  20260717✓  20260718✓  20260719✓
  slice-20260726-20260731  rrc13-rrc25    [pending  0/6]
     20260726·  20260727·  20260728·  20260729·  20260730·  20260731·

Status values: running, done, partial (some dates complete, session gone), pending.

docs.title: Collecting path files
docs.text:
Once nodes are done, collect from the central machine:

just date='202607*' collect          # all of July
just date='202607*' jobs=4 collect   # with more parallelism

date accepts glob patterns. Files already present locally are skipped (--ignore-existing). Per-host logs go to ./logs/collect-202607/<hostname>.log.

docs.title: Building the global topology
docs.text:
just date='202607*' topology          # combined + v4 + v6
just date='202607*' topology-combined # combined only

OOM on large datasets

build-topology.py defaults to cpu_count workers. On machines with many cores this can exhaust memory. Use workers to limit it: 

just date='202607*' workers=2 topology-combined

docs.title: Typical full-month workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Edit assignments.csv with the month's ranges and collector splits
#    (each line = one tmux session)

# 2. Dispatch from the central machine
just dispatch

# 3. Check progress periodically
just status

# 4. Once all done, collect and build
just date='202607*' jobs=4 collect
just date='202607*' workers=4 topology

docs.title: Fetching output files from remote machines
docs.text:
fleet/fetch-results.sh collects topology output files (not path files) from remote machines via rsync into per-host subdirectories. Configure SOURCES, INCLUDES, and EXCLUDE at the top of the script.

Legacy

fetch-results.sh predates the dispatch/collect workflow. It remains useful for ad-hoc collection without fleet.csv / assignments.csv.

docs.title: Installation & Dependencies
docs.text: This page lists every system-level dependency needed to run the pipeline. Python packages are managed automatically by uv — you do not install them by hand.

docs.title: Dependency overview
docs.text: Tool Role Pre-installed? bgpreader Parse MRT/bview files No — see below uv Python 3.12+ runtime + packages No just Pipeline task runner No bash 4+ Required for shell scripts macOS ships bash 3 python3 Date math in dispatch/status scripts Usually yes tmux Fleet dispatch (background sessions) Often yes on Linux rsync Path file collection across fleet Usually yes ssh (key-based) Fleet access — no password prompts Setup required

docs.title: Homebrew
docs.text:
All dependencies are available via Homebrew.

brew install bgpstream uv just bash tmux

bash 4+ is required

macOS ships with bash 3.2 (GPL2 license restriction). collect.sh and dispatch.sh use mapfile and export -f, which require bash 4+. After installing: 

# Verify the new bash is on PATH (Homebrew installs to /opt/homebrew/bin or /usr/local/bin)
bash --version          # should show 5.x
which bash              # /opt/homebrew/bin/bash
The scripts use #!/usr/bin/env bash, which will find the Homebrew bash if it is earlier on PATH than /bin/bash. If it isn't, add /opt/homebrew/bin to the front of PATH in your shell profile.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
Homebrew on LinuxUbuntu / Debian + uvFedora / RHEL

Homebrew runs on Linux and is the simplest path:

# Install Homebrew if you haven't already
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

brew install bgpstream uv just tmux

bgpstream has no official apt package — build from source:

# Build dependencies
sudo apt install -y build-essential libbz2-dev zlib1g-dev \
    libcurl4-openssl-dev liblzma-dev automake autoconf libtool

# libbgpstream (provides bgpreader)
git clone https://github.com/CAIDA/libbgpstream.git
cd libbgpstream
./autogen.sh
./configure
make -j$(nproc)
sudo make install
sudo ldconfig
cd ..

# Verify
bgpreader --help

uv (Python manager): 

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

just (task runner): 

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf \
    https://just.systems/install.sh | bash -s -- --to ~/.local/bin

tmux (fleet dispatch): 

sudo apt install -y tmux


# Build dependencies for bgpstream
sudo dnf install -y gcc gcc-c++ make automake autoconf libtool \
    bzip2-devel zlib-devel libcurl-devel xz-devel

# bgpstream from source (same as Ubuntu instructions above)

# uv
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# just
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf \
    https://just.systems/install.sh | bash -s -- --to ~/.local/bin

# tmux
sudo dnf install -y tmux

docs.title: Python packages
docs.text:
Once uv is installed, it manages Python 3.12 and all package dependencies automatically. No pip install needed:

# From the repo root — installs into .venv automatically on first run
uv run get-mrt.py --help

All scripts are invoked as uv run <script> — this is intentional and handles the venv transparently.

docs.title: Fleet: SSH key setup
docs.text:
The fleet dispatch, status, and collect scripts connect to remote machines via SSH without passwords. Set up key-based auth from the central machine to every node:

# Generate a key if you don't have one
ssh-keygen -t ed25519

# Copy to each fleet node
ssh-copy-id carlos@gauss.xt6labs.io
ssh-copy-id carlos@node2.example.com

# Verify (should not ask for a password)
ssh carlos@gauss.xt6labs.io "echo ok"

StrictHostKeyChecking=no is set in the SSH options used by the scripts, so new hosts are accepted automatically. If you prefer explicit host verification, pre-populate ~/.ssh/known_hosts using ssh-keyscan:

ssh-keyscan gauss.xt6labs.io >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
bgpreader --help          # bgpstream — should print usage
uv run get-mrt.py --help  # Python toolchain
just --list               # task runner
bash --version            # must be 4.x or 5.x
tmux -V                   # fleet dispatch

docs.title: Single machine, one date
docs.text:
The simplest way to run the full pipeline — downloads from all RIS collectors plus the default RouteViews subset, extracts paths, and builds combined + IPv4 + IPv6 topologies.

just date=20260101 collectors=rrc00-rrc25 pipeline

Variable order

just requires variable assignments before the recipe name: just date=20260101 pipeline ✓ just pipeline date=20260101 ✗

Output lands in ./output-combined/20260101/:

output-combined/20260101/
  topology-20260101.txt        # all-AF edge list
  topology-20260101-asns.txt   # unique ASN list
  topology-20260101-v4.txt     # IPv4 edge list
  topology-20260101-v4-asns.txt
  topology-20260101-v6.txt     # IPv6 edge list
  topology-20260101-v6-asns.txt

Each edge list line is a pair of zero-padded ASNs, sorted numerically within the pair and across all lines:

00000006 00022773
00001299 00003356
00001299 00022773

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
Run steps individually when you need to reprocess or debug:

# 1. Download RIS snapshots
just date=20260101 collectors=rrc00-rrc25 download

# 2. Download RouteViews snapshots
just date=20260101 download-routeviews

# 3. Extract AS paths from all downloaded files
just date=20260101 process

# 4. Build topology (combined + v4 + v6)
just date=20260101 topology

Or build only one address family:

just date=20260101 topology-v4

docs.title: Three dates, multiple collectors
docs.text:
for d in 20260101 20260201 20260301; do
  just date=$d collectors=rrc00-rrc25 pipeline
done

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:

  • Fleet Workflow — distribute processing across multiple machines
  • Analysis Tools — filter, convert, annotate, and analyze topologies

docs.title: RIS Collectors
docs.text:
RIPE RIS operates collectors rrc00 through rrc25. Use rrc00-rrc25 in --collectors to include all of them.

Collector Location rrc00 Amsterdam, NL rrc01 London, UK rrc03 Amsterdam, NL rrc04 Geneva, CH rrc05 Vienna, AT rrc06 Otemachi, JP rrc07 Stockholm, SE rrc10 Milan, IT rrc11 New York, US rrc12 Frankfurt, DE rrc13 Moscow, RU rrc14 Palo Alto, US rrc15 São Paulo, BR rrc16 Miami, US rrc18 Barcelona, ES rrc19 Johannesburg, ZA rrc20 Zurich, CH rrc21 Paris, FR rrc22 Bucharest, RO rrc23 Singapore, SG rrc24 Montevideo, UY rrc25 Amsterdam, NL

docs.title: RouteViews Collectors (default set)
docs.text:
The download-routeviews recipe uses a working subset of ~40 available collectors. Full index: https://www.routeviews.org/routeviews/index.php/collectors/

Collector ID Region route-views.amsix Europe (AMS-IX) namex.fco Europe (Rome) hkix.hkg Asia (Hong Kong) route-views.sg Asia (Singapore) route-views.chicago North America route-views2 North America pacwave.lax North America crix.sjo North America ix-br2.gru Latin America (São Paulo) route-views.rio Latin America (Rio) route-views.kixp Africa (Nairobi) route-views.perth Oceania

docs.title: Edge list (topology.txt)
docs.text:
One undirected edge per line. Both ASNs are plain integers (or zero-padded to 8 digits with --justify-output). The smaller ASN always appears first. Lines are sorted numerically by the first ASN, then the second.

6 22773
1299 3356
1299 22773

With --justify-output:

00000006 00022773
00001299 00003356
00001299 00022773

docs.title: ASN list (topology-asns.txt)
docs.text: One ASN per line, sorted numerically. Zero-padded if --justify-output was used.

docs.title: Path list (topology-paths.txt)
docs.text: One AS path per line (space-separated ASNs), sorted numerically by leading ASN. Written only when --paths is passed to build-topology.py.

docs.title: Annotated topology (topology-annotated.txt)
docs.text: Six columns per line: ASN1 ASN2 CC1 RIR1 CC2 RIR2. Country codes are lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. RIR names: arin, ripencc, apnic, lacnic, afrinic. Absent ASNs annotated as unknown unknown.

docs.title: NRO Delegated Stats
docs.text:
Used by --filter-registered in build-topology.py and by the geo-filter.py and annotate-topology.py graph analysis tools.

URL Latest https://ftp.ripe.net/pub/stats/ripencc/nro-stats/latest/nro-delegated-stats Historical https://ftp.ripe.net/pub/stats/ripencc/nro-stats/YYYYMMDD/nro-delegated-stats

Relevant statuses: assigned (keep), available / reserved (discard).

docs.title: bgpreader
docs.text:
bgpreader is the system binary used by extract-paths.py to parse MRT files. It handles both .gz and .bz2 inputs transparently.

Output is |-delimited. Relevant columns (0-indexed):

Column Field 1 Element type (R = RIB entry, B = block start — skip B lines) 9 Prefix (colon present → IPv6) 11 AS path

Only R lines are processed. The option to read a single file is rib-file:

bgpreader -d singlefile -o rib-file=<path>

docs.title: CAIDA AS Relationships
docs.text:
CAIDA publishes monthly AS relationship inferences derived from BGP data. The tool get-caida-peers.py uses these to extract peer-to-peer (p2p) edges.

URL Serial-2 index https://publicdata.caida.org/datasets/as-relationships/serial-2/ Serial-1 index https://publicdata.caida.org/datasets/as-relationships/serial-1/

File format (|-delimited, lines starting with # are comments):

AS1|AS2|rel          # serial-1
AS1|AS2|rel|source   # serial-2

Relationship codes: 0 = peer-to-peer, -1 = provider→customer. Only rel=0 is extracted.

Downloaded .bz2 files are cached in ./caida-cache/ (gitignored). Serial-2 is preferred; serial-1 is used as fallback for pre-2012 months.

docs.title: .gitignore summary
docs.text:
The following are gitignored and must not be committed:

Path Reason mrt/ Downloaded MRT files (large binary data) paths/ Extracted AS path files (large) output-combined/ Generated topology and peer output files caida-cache/ Cached CAIDA .bz2 downloads topology*.txt Any topology edge list at repo root nro-delegated-stats* Cached NRO stats fleet.csv Deployment-specific; copy from fleet/fleet.csv.example fetch/ Rsync staging from fetch-results.sh

docs.title: Analysis Tools
docs.text: The analysis/ directory contains tools for analysing and transforming topology files. All run via ./run.sh <tool> from the repo root (or directly as uv run analysis/<tool>).

docs.title: Tools at a glance
docs.text: Tool Input Output Purpose topology-to-gml.py .txt edge list .gml Convert to GML for Gephi/yEd gml-to-topology.py .gml .txt edge list Convert GML back to edge list topology-core.py .txt edge list .txt edge list Filter to high-degree nodes geo-filter.py .txt or .gml .txt + .gml Filter to one or more countries hubs.py .txt or .gml .txt hub list List high-degree ASNs annotate-topology.py .txt edge list .txt with CC+RIR Add country/RIR columns asn-presence.py *-asns-YYYYMMDD.txt files matrix .txt Day-by-day ASN presence matrix topology-ops.py two or more .txt files .txt edge list Set operations (union / difference) lookup-as.py ASN(s) table / TSV Look up ASN holder info via RIPEstat path-transit-freq.py path .txt[.gz] file freq .txt Count transit AS frequency

docs.title: Reduce before visualising
docs.text:
Large topologies (200k+ edges) are slow to render in Gephi. Filter to a core first:

# Keep only nodes with degree ≥ 10
./run.sh topology-core.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output-combined/20260101/topology-core10.txt \
  --min-degree 10

# Convert core to GML with enriched labels
./run.sh topology-to-gml.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-core10.txt \
  --enrich --min-degree 10

docs.title: Regional analysis
docs.text:
# Latin America topology
./run.sh geo-filter.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --countries ar,br,cl,co,mx,pe,uy,ve \
  --output output-combined/20260101/latam

# Annotate with country/RIR for further analysis
./run.sh annotate-topology.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --date 20260101

docs.title: Track ASN stability over time
docs.text:
# Build topologies for several dates, then build the presence matrix
./run.sh asn-presence.py \
  --input "output-combined/*/topology-*-asns.txt" \
  --output output-combined/asn-presence.txt

docs.title: hubs.py
docs.text:
Lists ASNs with degree ≥ --min-degree from a topology edge list or GML file. Degree is computed in a single pass for .txt input — no GML conversion required.

./run.sh hubs.py --input <file> --min-degree <N> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt/.txt.gz) or .gml --output input stem + -hubs.txt Output file --min-degree required Minimum degree threshold --wide off Two-column output (ASN degree), sorted by degree descending

Without --wide: one ASN per line, sorted numerically. With --wide: two columns sorted by degree descending — useful for ranking.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# List all ASNs with degree ≥ 100
./run.sh hubs.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 100

# Ranked by degree
./run.sh hubs.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 50 --wide

docs.title: annotate-topology.py
docs.text:
Enriches a topology edge list by appending four columns to each edge: cc1 rir1 cc2 rir2 — the country code and RIR for each ASN, sourced from the NRO delegated stats.

./run.sh annotate-topology.py --input <file> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt or .txt.gz) --output input stem + -annotated.txt Output file --date latest NRO stats snapshot date YYYYMMDD --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

Country codes are lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. RIR names: arin, ripencc, apnic, lacnic, afrinic. ASNs absent from the NRO file are annotated as unknown unknown.

Input sort order is preserved.

docs.title: Output format
docs.text:
6057 3359 uy lacnic us arin
174 1916 us arin br lacnic
64512 65001 unknown unknown unknown unknown

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Annotate with the NRO snapshot matching the topology date
./run.sh annotate-topology.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --date 20260101

# With zero-padding
./run.sh annotate-topology.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101-annotated.txt \
  --date 20260101 --justify-output

docs.title: asn-presence.py
docs.text:
Builds a day-by-day ASN presence matrix from {stem}-asns-YYYYMMDD.txt files produced by build-topology.py. One row per unique ASN, one column per date, values 0/1.

./run.sh asn-presence.py --input <glob> [--output <file>]
Flag Default Description --input required Glob matching *-asns-YYYYMMDD.txt files. Repeat for multiple globs. --output first matched file's directory / asn-presence.txt Output matrix file

The first line is a header: ASN YYYYMMDD YYYYMMDD …. ASNs are zero-padded to 8 digits.

Load in pandas:

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("asn-presence.txt", sep=r"\s+", index_col=0, dtype=int)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
./run.sh asn-presence.py \
  --input "output-combined/*/topology-*-asns.txt" \
  --output output-combined/asn-presence.txt

docs.title: topology-ops.py
docs.text:
Set operations on two or more topology edge list files. Both plain (6 22773) and zero-padded (00000006 00022773) formats are handled; comparison is always numeric.

./run.sh topology-ops.py --op <add|sub> --output <file> [--justify-output] FILE [FILE ...]
Argument Description FILE ... Two or more topology edge list files (positional) --op add Union — all edges present in any input file, deduplicated --op sub Difference — edges in the first file not present in any remaining file --output Output file --justify-output Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Merge three dates
./run.sh topology-ops.py --op add \
  --output output-combined/combined.txt --justify-output \
  output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  output-combined/20260201/topology-20260201.txt \
  output-combined/20260301/topology-20260301.txt

# Links present in January but gone by March
./run.sh topology-ops.py --op sub \
  --output output-combined/disappeared.txt \
  output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  output-combined/20260301/topology-20260301.txt

docs.title: lookup-as.py
docs.text:
Queries the RIPEstat Data API for one or more ASNs. Returns AS holder name, announced prefix count, last-seen timestamp, and announced status.

./run.sh lookup-as.py --asn <N>
./run.sh lookup-as.py --file <file>
cat asns.txt | ./run.sh lookup-as.py
Flag Default Description --asn — Single ASN to look up --file — File with one ASN per line; - for stdin --output — Write results as TSV alongside terminal output --concurrency 10 Max parallel API requests (batch mode)

Batch mode shows a live progress bar. Results are displayed as a rich table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Single ASN
./run.sh lookup-as.py --asn 15169

# Batch from the dropped-ASNs list
./run.sh lookup-as.py \
  --file output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101-dropped-asns.txt \
  --output output-combined/20260101/dropped-asns-info.tsv

# Pipe the hub list
./run.sh hubs.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 100 | ./run.sh lookup-as.py

docs.title: path-transit-freq.py
docs.text:
Counts how often each AS appears as a transit hop across all paths in a file. The first ASN (sensor) and last ASN (origin) of each path are ignored; intermediate ASNs are deduplicated per path to collapse prepends.

./run.sh path-transit-freq.py --input <file> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Path file (.txt or .txt.gz) --output input stem + -transit-freq.txt Output file --justify-output / --no-justify-output on Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

Output is sorted by frequency descending. Paths with ≤2 ASNs (no transit hop) are skipped and counted; the total is reported on exit.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Analyse a combined path file
./run.sh path-transit-freq.py \
  --input paths/20260101/combined/bview.rrc00.20260101.0000.txt.gz

# Without zero-padding
./run.sh path-transit-freq.py \
  --input paths/20260101/combined/bview.rrc00.20260101.0000.txt.gz \
  --no-justify-output

docs.title: Conversion Tools
docs.text: Tools for converting between topology edge list format and GML.

docs.title: topology-to-gml.py
docs.text:
Converts a topology edge list (.txt) to a GML file for import into Gephi, yEd, Cytoscape, or any graph tool that reads GML.

./run.sh topology-to-gml.py --input <file> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt or .txt.gz) --output input with .gml extension Output GML file --min-degree 3 Filter: only include edges where both endpoints have degree ≥ N --enrich off Fetch AS holder names from RIPEstat and use as node labels --enrich-min-degree 3 Only enrich nodes with degree ≥ N (cheaper than enriching all nodes)

When --enrich is active, holder names are fetched from the RIPEstat API and cached at ~/.cache/internet-topology-ris/as-names.json with a 60-day TTL. Nodes below --enrich-min-degree keep their ASN as label.

To produce a filtered edge list (.txt) rather than a GML, use topology-core.py instead.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Basic conversion, no filtering
./run.sh topology-to-gml.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt

# Filter to core (degree ≥ 5) + enrich labels for well-connected nodes
./run.sh topology-to-gml.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output-combined/20260101/topology-core5.gml \
  --min-degree 5 \
  --enrich --enrich-min-degree 20

docs.title: gml-to-topology.py
docs.text:
Inverse of topology-to-gml.py. Reads a GML file and writes a two-column topology edge list. Useful for round-tripping through Gephi (e.g. after manual layout or community detection).

./run.sh gml-to-topology.py --input <file> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required GML file --output input with .txt extension Output edge list --min-degree (none) Optional: filter to edges where both endpoints have degree ≥ N --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

ASNs are always read from the node asn attribute (safe for enriched GML files that carry string labels).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Round-trip: convert back from Gephi export
./run.sh gml-to-topology.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-gephi.gml \
  --output output-combined/20260101/topology-gephi.txt

# With degree filter
./run.sh gml-to-topology.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology.gml \
  --min-degree 10 \
  --justify-output

docs.title: topology-core.py
docs.text:
Filters a topology edge list to edges where both endpoints have degree ≥ --min-degree. Produces a valid topology file in the same two-column format.

Useful before visualisation (large topologies are slow in Gephi) or before analysis steps you want to run only on well-connected ASNs.

./run.sh topology-core.py --input <file> --min-degree <N> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt or .txt.gz) --output input stem + -core.txt Output filtered edge list --min-degree required Minimum degree (both endpoints must qualify) --wide off Add DEG1 DEG2 columns to the output --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

Degree is computed from the input file directly — no GML conversion required.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Keep only edges where both ASNs have degree ≥ 10
./run.sh topology-core.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 10

# Same, but annotate with degrees and zero-pad
./run.sh topology-core.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output-combined/20260101/topology-core10.txt \
  --min-degree 10 --wide --justify-output

docs.title: geo-filter.py
docs.text:
Filters a topology to edges where both ASNs are assigned to one of the given ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, according to the NRO delegated stats. ASNs absent from the NRO file are excluded.

Always produces two output files:

  • {output}.txt — filtered edge list
  • {output}.gml — filtered graph with a country node attribute
./run.sh geo-filter.py --input <file> --countries <cc,...> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt/.txt.gz) or .gml --countries required Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (lowercase) --output input stem + -geo Base output path (no extension — both .txt and .gml written) --date latest NRO stats snapshot date YYYYMMDD for reproducible filtering --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

NRO stats are fetched and cached next to the input file.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Latin American topology
./run.sh geo-filter.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --countries ar,br,cl,co,mx,pe,uy,ve \
  --output output-combined/20260101/latam \
  --date 20260101

# Single country
./run.sh geo-filter.py \
  --input output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --countries br \
  --output output-combined/20260101/brazil

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
The pipeline is a linear three-step process orchestrated by just.

get-mrt.py          ──┐
                       ├──▶  extract-paths.py  ──▶  build-topology.py
get-routeviews.py   ──┘

./mrt/<date>/       ──▶  ./paths/<date>/            ──▶  ./output-combined/<date>/
  *.gz (RIS)              combined/*.txt.gz
  *.bz2 (RouteViews)      v4/*.v4.txt.gz
                          v6/*.v6.txt.gz

docs.title: Justfile recipes
docs.text: Recipe What it runs pipeline download + download-routeviews + process + topology download get-mrt.py for the given collectors download-routeviews get-routeviews.py for the default RouteViews subset process extract-paths.py on all .gz and .bz2 files topology topology-combined + topology-v4 + topology-v6 topology-combined build-topology.py on combined path files topology-v4 build-topology.py on IPv4 path files topology-v6 build-topology.py on IPv6 path files slice download + download-routeviews + process (self-contained, for fleet nodes) dispatch dispatch slice jobs to all fleet nodes via assignments.csv + fleet.csv status report per-date progress for all assigned fleet nodes collect rsync path files from all fleet nodes caida-peers get-caida-peers.py for the given month pack-and-publish tar + copy to a publish point

docs.title: Justfile variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description date (empty) Snapshot date YYYYMMDD. Required for download and topology. collectors rrc00 RIS collector spec — individual, list, or range (e.g. rrc00-rrc25). mrt_dir ./mrt Root for downloaded MRT files. Date subdir created automatically. paths_dir ./paths Root for extracted path files. Date subdir created automatically. output_dir ./output-combined Root for topology output. Date subdir created automatically. output topology-<date>.txt Combined output filename. output_v4 topology-<date>-v4.txt IPv4 output filename. output_v6 topology-<date>-v6.txt IPv6 output filename. jobs 2 Parallel connections for collect and dispatch. workers (empty) Worker count for build-topology.py (topology recipes). Omit for cpu_count. Set low (e.g. 2) to avoid OOM on large datasets. paths (empty) Set to any non-empty value (e.g. 1) to write a consolidated paths file from topology-combined. Checkpoint/resume aware (.paths.gz sidecars). no_justify (empty) Set to any non-empty value (e.g. 1) to disable zero-padding in caida-peers. pubpoint /var/www/html/topo Destination for pack-and-publish.

docs.title: Pages in this section
docs.text:
• Download — get-mrt.py and get-routeviews.py
  • Extract Paths — extract-paths.py
  • Build Topology — build-topology.py
  • CAIDA Peers — get-caida-peers.py

docs.title: CAIDA AS Relationships
docs.text:
get-caida-peers.py downloads the CAIDA AS Relationships dataset for a given month and extracts all peer-to-peer edges (relationship code 0). The result is a deduplicated, sorted two-column edge list in the same format as the BGP-derived topology.

./run.sh get-caida-peers.py --date YYYYMM [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Default Description --date required Year-month to fetch, YYYYMM format --output ./output-combined/YYYYMM/caida-peers-YYYYMM.txt Output file path --justify-output / --no-justify-output on Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits --cache-dir ./caida-cache Where to store downloaded .bz2 files

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
CAIDA publishes two dataset series, both available at no cost:

Series Coverage File pattern serial-2 ~2012 – present YYYYMMDD.as-rel2.txt.bz2 serial-1 ~1998 – 2013 YYYYMMDD.as-rel.txt.bz2

The tool prefers serial-2. If no serial-2 file exists for the requested month (pre-2012 data), it falls back to serial-1. File names within a month are not predictable (not always the 1st of the month), so the tool fetches the directory index to discover the correct filename.

docs.title: Relationship codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning Included? 0 Peer-to-peer ✓ -1 Provider → customer ✗

Only rel=0 edges are written to output. Provider-customer relationships are discarded.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Downloaded .bz2 files are cached permanently in --cache-dir (default ./caida-cache/, gitignored). CAIDA files are immutable once published — a cached file is always reused without re-downloading.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Two files are always written to the same directory:

File Contents caida-peers-YYYYMM.txt Peer-to-peer edge list (rel=0) caida-tier1-YYYYMM.txt Potential Tier 1 ASNs — one ASN per line

docs.title: Peer edge list
docs.text:
One undirected edge per line, smaller ASN first, sorted numerically:

00000001 00005467
00000001 00008641
00001299 00003356

docs.title: Potential Tier 1 list
docs.text:
ASNs that provide transit to others (appear as provider in a rel=-1 relationship) but never buy transit themselves (never appear as customer). These are provider-free transit networks — the operational definition of Tier 1.

00000174
00000701
00001299
00003356

The list typically contains ~100–200 ASNs: the ~20 globally recognised Tier 1 networks plus regional/national networks that are provider-free in their own market. Networks that are widely considered Tier 1 but appear as a customer in at least one CAIDA-inferred relationship (e.g. Hurricane Electric, AS6939) will be absent.

Plain integers (no zero-padding) with --no-justify-output.

docs.title: Justfile
docs.text:
# Fetch peer relationships for a month
just date=202401 caida-peers

# Without zero-padding
just date=202401 no_justify=1 caida-peers

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# January 2024 — uses serial-2
./run.sh get-caida-peers.py --date 202401

# January 2005 — falls back to serial-1
./run.sh get-caida-peers.py --date 200501

# Override output path, no zero-padding
./run.sh get-caida-peers.py \
  --date 202401 \
  --output ./my-peers-202401.txt \
  --no-justify-output

docs.title: Download
docs.text: Two scripts handle downloading, one per data source. Both follow the same interface and produce files in the same output directory; extract-paths.py handles both transparently.

docs.title: get-mrt.py — RIPE RIS
docs.text:
Downloads the 00:00 UTC RIB snapshot (bview) for a given date from one or more RIS collectors. Already-downloaded files are skipped. Failed transfers are reported per-collector and counted in the summary without aborting the run.

./run.sh get-mrt.py --collectors <spec> --date <YYYYMMDD> [--output-dir <dir>]
Flag Required Description --collectors yes Collector specification (see below) --date yes Snapshot date in YYYYMMDD format --output-dir no Output directory. Default: ./mrt

Output filenames: bview.rrcXX.YYYYMMDD.0000.gz

docs.title: Collector specification
docs.text:
--collectors accepts a comma-separated mix of individual names and ranges:

Syntax Example Expands to Individual rrc00 rrc00 List rrc00,rrc04,rrc11 rrc00, rrc04, rrc11 Range rrc00-rrc05 rrc00 through rrc05 Mixed rrc00-rrc03,rrc11 rrc00–rrc03, rrc11

RIS has collectors rrc00 through rrc25. Use rrc00-rrc25 to collect from all of them.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# All collectors
just date=20260101 collectors=rrc00-rrc25 download

# Single collector
./run.sh get-mrt.py --collectors rrc00 --date 20260101

# Mixed specification
./run.sh get-mrt.py --collectors rrc00-rrc05,rrc11,rrc23 --date 20260101 --output-dir ./mrt/20260101

docs.title: get-routeviews.py — RouteViews
docs.text:
Same interface as get-mrt.py but targets the RouteViews archive. Output files are .bz2 format.

./run.sh get-routeviews.py --collectors <list> --date <YYYYMMDD> [--output-dir <dir>]
Flag Required Description --collectors yes Comma-separated RouteViews collector IDs --date yes Snapshot date in YYYYMMDD format --output-dir no Output directory. Default: ./mrt

Output filenames: rib.<collector>.YYYYMMDD.0000.bz2

RouteViews collectors do not follow a numeric sequence, so range notation is not supported — use a comma-separated list.

docs.title: Default collector set
docs.text:
The download-routeviews justfile recipe uses a working subset of the ~40 available collectors:

Collector ID Region route-views.amsix Europe (AMS-IX) namex.fco Europe (Rome) hkix.hkg Asia (Hong Kong) route-views.sg Asia (Singapore) route-views.chicago North America route-views2 North America pacwave.lax North America crix.sjo North America ix-br2.gru Latin America (São Paulo) route-views.rio Latin America (Rio) route-views.kixp Africa (Nairobi) route-views.perth Oceania

To add more, extend the --collectors argument in the download-routeviews recipe in the justfile. Full collector index: https://www.routeviews.org/routeviews/index.php/collectors/

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Default subset via justfile
just date=20260101 download-routeviews

# Custom selection
./run.sh get-routeviews.py \
  --collectors route-views.amsix,route-views2,route-views.sg \
  --date 20260101 \
  --output-dir ./mrt/20260101

docs.title: Downloading a full month of RouteViews data
docs.text:
download-routeviews-month.sh downloads one bview per day for an entire month, running up to N days in parallel:

./fleet/download-routeviews-month.sh YYYYMM [parallel_jobs]

# Download all of January 2026, 4 days in parallel
./fleet/download-routeviews-month.sh 202601 4

Output: ./mrt-routeviews/YYYYMMDD/ Logs: ./logs/routeviews-YYYYMM/YYYYMMDD.log

docs.title: Extract Paths
docs.text:
extract-paths.py calls bgpreader on each MRT file and writes three sidecar files per input — one combined, one IPv4-only, one IPv6-only — into address-family subdirectories. A file set is skipped only if all three outputs already exist.

./run.sh extract-paths.py --input-files <glob> [--output-dir <dir>]
Flag Required Description --input-files yes Glob pattern matching MRT files (.gz or .bz2) --output-dir no Root output directory. Default: ./paths

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Output is written into three subdirectories under --output-dir. The filename strips the source extension (.gz or .bz2) and appends a suffix:

Subdirectory Suffix Contents combined/ .txt.gz All paths (combined IPv4 + IPv6) v4/ .v4.txt.gz IPv4-only paths v6/ .v6.txt.gz IPv6-only paths

For example: bview.rrc00.20260101.0000.gz → - combined/bview.rrc00.20260101.0000.txt.gz - v4/bview.rrc00.20260101.0000.v4.txt.gz - v6/bview.rrc00.20260101.0000.v6.txt.gz

Checkpoint sidecars (.edges, .paths.gz) written by build-topology.py also live in combined/, next to their source files.

Address family is detected from the prefix field (column 9 in bgpreader output): a colon (:) in the prefix indicates IPv6.

Output files are gzip-compressed (.txt.gz). build-topology.py detects this automatically via magic bytes.

docs.title: Path cleaning rules
docs.text:
Applied before writing each path:

  • Prepend removal — consecutive duplicate ASNs are collapsed: 64500 64500 64501 → 64500 64501
  • AS set truncation — paths containing AS sets (e.g. {64500,64501}) are truncated at that point; edges before the set are kept

docs.title: Justfile
docs.text:
The process recipe runs twice — once for .gz files (RIS) and once for .bz2 files (RouteViews):

just date=20260101 process

If no files match a glob, the invocation prints a notice and exits cleanly (not an error).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Process all RIS files for a date
./run.sh extract-paths.py \
  --input-files "./mrt/20260101/*.gz" \
  --output-dir ./paths/20260101
# Writes: paths/20260101/combined/*.txt.gz
#         paths/20260101/v4/*.v4.txt.gz
#         paths/20260101/v6/*.v6.txt.gz

# Process all RouteViews files for the same date
./run.sh extract-paths.py \
  --input-files "./mrt/20260101/*.bz2" \
  --output-dir ./paths/20260101

docs.title: Build Topology
docs.text:
build-topology.py reads AS path files, extracts edges, deduplicates, and writes the topology. It accepts multiple --input globs and merges RIS and RouteViews files seamlessly. Workers process files in parallel.

./run.sh build-topology.py --input <glob> [--input <glob> ...] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Default Description --input required Glob matching path .txt files. Repeat to add more patterns. --output ./topology.txt Output file for the edge list. --date (none) Snapshot date YYYYMMDD. Required when using --filter-registered with a historical NRO snapshot. --filter-registered off Exclude paths containing any non-assigned ASN (see below). --justify-output off Zero-pad all ASNs to 8 digits in all output files. --paths off Also write a deduplicated path list {stem}-paths.txt. Large and expensive; off by default. Checkpoint/resume aware — writes .paths.gz sidecars alongside .edges. --workers cpu_count Number of parallel worker processes. --keep-edges off Retain .edges and .paths.gz checkpoint sidecars after a successful merge (useful to re-run with different flags without reprocessing).

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
All files are written to the same directory as --output, named after its stem.

File Description {stem}.txt Deduplicated undirected edge list. One AS1 AS2 per line, AS1 < AS2, sorted numerically. {stem}-asns.txt Sorted list of all unique ASNs in the topology. {stem}-paths.txt (only with --paths) Deduplicated AS paths, sorted numerically by leading ASN. {stem}-dropped-asns.txt (only with --filter-registered) ASNs excluded because they are not assigned in the NRO stats.

docs.title: --filter-registered
docs.text:
Filters at the path level: a path is excluded entirely if any of its ASNs is not assigned in the NRO delegated extended stats. This removes paths transiting unallocated, reserved, or private ASNs.

The NRO stats file is cached next to the input path files:

  • Historical (when --date is provided): nro-delegated-stats-YYYYMMDD — fetched once and cached permanently (the historical file never changes).
  • Latest (no --date): nro-delegated-stats — re-downloaded if older than 24 hours.

docs.title: --justify-output
docs.text:
Zero-pads all ASN numbers to 8 digits in every output file, making them fixed-width:

# Without --justify-output   # With --justify-output
6 22773                       00000006 00022773
1299 3356                     00001299 00003356

Fixed-width output is useful for lexicographic sorting tools and for consistent alignment in downstream processing.

docs.title: Edge ordering
docs.text: Edges are stored as integer-ordered tuples: the smaller ASN always comes first. String ordering is not used — "22773" < "6" as strings but 22773 > 6 as integers.

docs.title: Justfile
docs.text:
The topology recipe runs build-topology.py three times (combined, v4, v6):

just date=20260101 topology

# Individual variants
just date=20260101 topology-combined
just date=20260101 topology-v4
just date=20260101 topology-v6

# With consolidated paths file (combined only)
just date=20260101 paths=1 topology-combined

# Limit workers to avoid OOM on large datasets
just date='202607*' workers=4 topology-combined

# Glob date — all of July
just date='202607*' topology

docs.title: Justfile variables for topology
docs.text: Variable Default Description workers (empty = cpu_count) Worker count for build-topology.py. Set lower to avoid OOM. paths (empty = off) Set to any non-empty value (e.g. 1) to write a consolidated path file for topology-combined.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Combined topology from a single date (RIS + RouteViews)
./run.sh build-topology.py \
  --input "./paths/20260101/combined/*.txt.gz" \
  --output ./output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --filter-registered \
  --justify-output \
  --date 20260101

# Also write the path list, use 8 workers
./run.sh build-topology.py \
  --input "./paths/20260101/combined/*.txt.gz" \
  --output ./output-combined/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --paths \
  --workers 8
